faqs.q: What do the 100, 440, 1000 and 8000 Hz tones mean?

speaker-test.formula:
Tone = a sine wave at one fixed frequency, played for 5 seconds.
Sweep = a sine wave gliding from 200 Hz to 8000 Hz over 20 seconds.
Left = sound only in the left channel. Right = only the right channel.
Center = equal sound in both channels (mono).
howTo: Pick a channel: Left, Right, or Center (both).
Choose a test frequency - 440 Hz is a good starting point.
Set the volume low, then press Play tone.
For a full check, press Play sweep and listen from 200 Hz to 8000 Hz.
If one side is silent or much quieter, check your cable and balance settings.
keyFacts: Left and right channel tests prove each speaker (or headphone driver) receives its own signal.
A pure 440 Hz tone is the musical note A - your reference point for normal hearing.
The 20-second sweep glides from 200 Hz (bass) to 8000 Hz (treble) so you can hear drop-outs.
Small laptop and phone speakers often fade below 300 Hz and above 6000 Hz - that is normal physics, not a fault.
Test tones are generated live in your browser with the Web Audio API - no audio files needed.
Start quiet and raise the volume slowly; high-frequency tones can be uncomfortable at full volume.

limitations: This page cannot measure true loudness in decibels - only what you hear.
It cannot detect distortion at high volumes the way a microphone measurement could.
Phone and laptop speakers are physically limited; weak bass there is expected.
Browser autoplay policies mean you must press a button - tones never start by themselves.

speaker-test.quickAnswer: A speaker test plays test tones through your speakers or headphones. The Left and Right buttons send sound to one side only, Center sends it to both, and the frequency sweep glides from 200 Hz to 8000 Hz over 20 seconds. If you hear the left tone only on the left, your stereo setup is correct. A silent side means a dead speaker, loose cable, or wrong balance setting.
speaker-test.tagline: Play left/right test tones and a full frequency sweep to check your speakers and headphones.
speaker-test.workedExample:
You test a new pair of headphones:
1. You pick Right and play the 440 Hz tone. You hear it only in the right ear - correct.
2. You pick Left. The tone moves to the left ear - the channels are not swapped.
3. You play the sweep. The sound glides smoothly upward; around 7000 Hz it gets quieter, which is normal for small drivers.
4. No crackling at any point, so the drivers are healthy.
